claims.text: Rapid induction melting produces a non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution state.
The initial solid solution is supersaturated in Mg and contains minor incipient intermetallic phases.
The proposed alloy has an overall density below 6 g/cm³.
The metastable state gradually destabilizes through diffusion-controlled Mg segregation.
Mg segregation promotes nucleation and coarsening of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds at grain boundaries and within the matrix.
Formation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds locally depletes the surrounding matrix of Mg.
The resulting compositional heterogeneity changes oxide-scale formation and adhesion at high temperature.
Intermetallic–matrix heterogeneity enhances microgalvanic coupling and thereby modifies corrosion behavior.
Isothermal aging at 600–800 °C permits diffusion-driven phase separation in the alloy.
Mg has a higher diffusivity than the other constituents of the proposed HEA.
Preferential Mg diffusion drives segregation from the supersaturated matrix and subsequent growth of stable Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
The evolved local chemistry may promote less adherent or non-protective MgO scales.
Microgalvanic effects between Mg-rich intermetallics and the matrix accelerate localized corrosion.
Aged samples will have a larger volume fraction of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds than as-cast samples.
Mg-rich intermetallic compounds will coarsen during aging.
Aging-induced phase evolution will produce thinner or less adherent protective oxide layers than in the as-cast condition.
Aging-induced phase evolution will cause measurable corrosion changes, including localized attack associated with microgalvanic coupling.
The as-cast alloy has moderate corrosion and oxidation behavior.
Differences in constituent properties favor formation of stable intermetallic compounds during aging.
Absence of a statistically significant intermetallic-phase change, or absence of correlation between that change and oxidation or corrosion behavior, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as containing minor incipient intermetallic phases, whereas the baseline is described as a homogeneous metastable solid-solution microstructure. The intended tolerance for second phases is not clarified.
